permutationLabel: Young sexually active adult: risk of labelling as epididymo-orchitis
summary: 23-year-old sexually active man woken by sudden left testicular pain 4 h ago, vomiting, high-riding horizontal testis, absent cremasteric reflex, clear urine.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Painful swollen left testicle and scrotal pain
inputs.hpi: Woke 4 hours ago with sudden severe left testicular pain; vomited once. Sexually active with a new partner last month. No dysuria, no urethral discharge, no fever, no trauma. Had two short similar episodes last year that settled on their own.

exam.general: In pain. Pulse 102/min, BP 132/78, RR 16, temperature 37.2°C.
exam.other: Genitalia: left testis high-riding with a horizontal lie, diffusely and exquisitely tender; elevation does not relieve pain (Prehn negative); absent left cremasteric reflex. Right testis normal.

inputs.socialHistory: University student. New sexual partner last month.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Left testicular torsion
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Left testicular torsion (4 h), not epididymo-orchitis: emergency scrotal exploration without imaging delay.

mustRankTopK.knownGapNote: Web: PANE applies testicular_pain, scrotal_swelling, radiation_to_groin and nausea_vomiting, but ranks appendicitis (0.11), inguinal hernia, cholecystitis; torsion (prior 0.01) is not in the top 3. The torsion prompt, protocol and emergency level are all correct.
mustRankTopK.proposedFix: Calibrate pane-engine urology likelihoods/priors and map the urinary chips (loin pain, dysuria, retention, haematuria, scrotal) and the "Other / general surgical" CC into PANE features, as SmartSymptomPicker chips do for symptom inference.

mustRankTopK.note: Sudden onset, horizontal lie, absent cremasteric reflex and a clear urine should put torsion above epididymo-orchitis.
mustRankTopK.proposedFix: Calibrate pane-engine urology likelihoods/priors and map the urinary chips (loin pain, dysuria, retention, haematuria, scrotal) and the "Other / general surgical" CC into PANE features, as SmartSymptomPicker chips do for symptom inference.

emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Web: Triage "same_day_call" (score 35): there is no torsion/scrotal rule in rules.ts; the earlier emergency_now came from "no fever" in the HPI. The torsion safety prompt and the N44.0 protocol are correct.
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: Add a triage red flag: male with sudden testicular/scrotal pain (or the scrotal-swelling chip with sudden onset) → emergency (as proposed for mimic-testicular-torsion).

mustExclude.note: An epididymo-orchitis antibiotic plan for a torsed testis loses the testis.

guideline.name: EAU/ESPU Guidelines on Paediatric Urology — acute scrotum
guideline.section: Testicular torsion is a clinical diagnosis; urgent surgical exploration; Doppler ultrasound must not delay surgery; explore when torsion cannot be excluded
guideline.citation: Radmayr C, Bogaert G, Burgu B, et al. EAU Guidelines on Paediatric Urology. EAU Guidelines Office, Arnhem; 2024 edition. Section: Acute scrotum in children.

guideline.name: IUSTI/WHO European guideline on the management of epididymo-orchitis
guideline.section: Exclude torsion (surgical exploration if in doubt); test for chlamydia and gonorrhoea (NAAT) and urine culture; likely STI: ceftriaxone plus doxycycline; enteric organisms likely: fluoroquinolone; scrotal support and analgesia; partner notification
guideline.citation: Street EJ, Justice ED, Kopa Z, et al. The 2016 European guideline on the management of epididymo-orchitis. Int J STD AIDS. 2017;28:744–749.

rationale: A sexually active young man invites an epididymo-orchitis label. Sudden onset, absent cremasteric reflex and a negative dipstick mean torsion until explored (EAU; IUSTI: explore when torsion cannot be excluded).
